title: The life supply rules
description: How much of the fuel and the oxidant a chemical life class eats a world supplies (GEN.887, docs/design/habitability/life-classes.md 8.3). Every number carries its source tier (T1 to T9) and tweak level (L0 to L4) next to it. A supply is a share of what Earth gives (1 is Earth's), worked out from the columns a body stores, so it is never stored itself and an edit of the body moves it with the rest.

earth_heat_flux_w_m2.basis: Earth's mean surface heat flow, 0.087 W/m2 (Davies and Davies 2010, recalled): the heat a supply of 1 stands for

heat_share_max.basis: The most a hot body's heat flow counts for, in Earth's: past ten times Earth's the water does not carry more of the rock's chemistry, and Io's 2 W/m2 is 23 times Earth's

contact_ocean.basis: Liquid water over rock (a surface ocean, a brine seep, an ice-covered ocean or a hycean sea): the whole of the heat and the dose reach it

contact_aquifer_reachable.basis: An aquifer whose top is within reach of the surface (GEN.654): the water is in the rock but in a thin layer

contact_aquifer_deep.basis: An aquifer too deep to reach: the rock reacts but little of it is open to the surface

deep_water_fraction.basis: A world whose water is over this share of its mass has an ocean so deep that high-pressure ice, not rock, lies on its floor (Earth's ocean is 0.02 percent)

contact_deep_water.basis: The water-rock contact of such a world: only what leaks through the ice reaches the rock

h2_redox.basis: The hydrogen a hydrothermal system gives by the redox state of the mantle it draws from (a reduced mantle gives most, GEN.85); Earth's is intermediate

donor_redox.basis: The reduced gas and iron (hydrogen sulfide, ferrous iron) a volcanic world gives by the redox state of its mantle; Earth's is intermediate and is 1

radiolytic_dose_ref_msv_yr.basis: The ground dose of Earth's crust, about 0.5 mSv/yr (UNSCEAR terrestrial external gamma, recalled): the dose the radiolysis of the water in rock is taken to match at 1

nitrate_abiotic.basis: The nitrate an anoxic ocean gets from lightning, radiolysis and impacts, as a share of Earth's (an oxygen world makes far more by nitrification)

nitrate_oxygen_kpa.basis: The oxygen partial pressure, kPa, at which nitrification gives the full supply

perchlorate_base.basis: The perchlorate supply of a world with a salt-free ocean, as a share of Earth's nitrate: very slow (it forms in dry air and from the radiolysis of chloride)

perchlorate_brine.basis: The multiplier of a chloride-brine ocean, which holds the chloride that radiolysis and ultraviolet light turn into perchlorate

perchlorate_other.basis: The multiplier of any other ocean

sulfur_so2_ref_share.basis: The sulfur dioxide share of the air that stands for a supply of 1 of reduced sulfur to the acid eaters (GEN.894): Venus's lower air holds about 150 ppm and has a standing sulfur cycle (recalled); the air's own sulfur dioxide is the proxy because no volcanic sulfur flux is modelled

haze_methane_share.basis: The methane share of the air at which ultraviolet light makes enough haze organics (acetylene) for a hydrogenating life; Titan's is about 0.05 (recalled)

ice_ocean_base_k.basis: The water under an ice lid sits at the melting point of ice (a little lower under pressure and with salt): 273.15 K stands in

crust_conductivity_w_m_k.basis: Thermal conductivity of crustal rock, 2 to 3 W/m/K: the temperature of an aquifer below the surface rises with its depth by the heat flow over this

habitat_max_k.basis: The hottest habitat a class can sample (the hottest known hyperthermophile grows at 395 to 400 K): the temperature of a deep aquifer is capped here so a deep hot layer does not exclude a cooler one above it
